title: Hold Still
status: concept-proposal (Creative Director, 2026-11-19; not approved; awaiting owner review)
hook_line: Night mode says hold still. Now I know why.
first_visual: A phone screen in a dark bedroom counting down over a blurred room, one sharp shape in the corner.

beats.visual: Phone UI 'Hold still 3...' over a blurred room; one sharp shape in the corner.
beats.vo: Night mode says hold still. Now I know why.

beats.visual: Jun in bed lifts his phone toward the moon in the window.
beats.vo: I was just shooting the moon.

beats.visual: The photo result: the room smeared, a tall figure in the corner perfectly sharp.
beats.vo: Long exposure blurs anything that moves. Not this.

beats.visual: Jun lowers the phone; the corner is empty; he raises it again.
beats.vo: The corner's empty. Second photo: closer.

beats.visual: Third result: Jun blurred, the figure sharp, head tilted over his shoulder.
beats.vo: Third. I'm the blur. It's right behind me.

beats.visual: Push-in: Jun frozen, eyes wide, not breathing.
beats.vo: It only moves when I move. So I don't.

beats.visual: Key moment: a long Ash-Violet finger enters frame and taps Jun's phone screen.
Final photo: Jun and the figure, both sharp, side by side; moth on the phone wallpaper.

ending: Final photo: Jun and the tall figure, both sharp, side by side, posed like friends.
loop_note: Yes. The final photo cuts back to the opening countdown; on a second viewing the 'sharp shape' in frame 1 is recognisable.

originality_review: Original. The long-exposure 'stillness' rule is our own mechanic. It does not use the tropes of a ghost in a photo that vanishes or a face in the background. Different from MW010 (face unlock).
scores_basis: Initial editorial judgement, 2026-11-19. topic_demand is an estimate linked to research/WEEKLY_TREND_REPORT.md categories, not a measurement of this concept.
concept: A teen's night-mode photos blur everything that moves. One tall figure stays razor-sharp and closer each shot, because it only moves when he does. His stillness gives it the photo it wanted.

hooks.line: Night mode says hold still. Now I know why.
hooks.first_visual: A phone screen in a dark bedroom counting down over a blurred room, one sharp shape in the corner.

hooks.line: Everything in my photo was blurry except it.
hooks.first_visual: A long-exposure photo: smeared room, one perfectly crisp tall figure.

hooks.line: Three photos. Each time it's closer.
hooks.first_visual: Three thumbnails side by side, a shape advancing.

hooks.line: Long exposure blurs anything that moves. Except this.
hooks.first_visual: A shaking hand holding a phone up to a window.

hooks.line: It only moves when I move. So I didn't.
hooks.first_visual: A teenager frozen in bed, eyes wide, the warm highlight trembling.

setting: Jun's bedroom at night; moon through the window; the phone camera UI.
conflict: Jun must work out the rule of the thing in his photos before it reaches him.
escalation: Corner, then the foot of the bed, then directly behind him.
reveal: He holds perfectly still. A long grey finger presses the shutter for him.
emotional_objective: Paranoia, then the helplessness of obeying.
